overall: The AG found violations for late OML certification forms, untimely approval of minutes, insufficient July 25, 2023 minutes, and a pre-meeting deliberation (remedied); other allegations were not violations or were declined.

allegations.summary: Board members did not timely complete Open Meeting Law certification forms within two weeks of qualifying for office.
allegations.key_passage: The Board acknowledges that members did not timely complete the Open Meeting Law certification form and therefore we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Board failed to approve open session minutes of meetings held January 10 to July 25, 2023, in a timely manner.
allegations.key_passage: The Board acknowledges, and we find, that the Board did not approve minutes of the thirteen meetings held between January 10, 2023, and July 25, 2023, within the later of the next three meetings or 30 days following each meeting.

allegations.summary: Minutes of the July 25, 2023 meeting were alleged to be insufficient, omitting discussion, votes, and a commenter's remarks.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the minutes do not adequately capture the substance of the discussions that occurred so that a member of the public who did not attend the meeting could read the minutes and have an understanding of what occurred

allegations.summary: Generalized complaint that Board meeting minutes are generally insufficient and missing key information, without identifying specific minutes.
allegations.key_passage: With respect to the concerns raised in the first complaint that meeting minutes are generally insufficient, we will not conduct broad audits of a public body based on generalized allegations.

allegations.summary: Second complaint alleged the September 12, 2023 minutes were insufficient, but it was filed more than 30 days after the minutes were approved.
allegations.key_passage: Because the complaint here was filed on December 15, 2023, more than 30 days after the date that the Board approved the September 12, 2023, minutes, we find this allegation to be untimely and decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly held an unposted 'organizational meeting' in February 2023 where members deliberated, requiring notice and minutes.
allegations.key_passage: Absent evidence to the contrary, we find that the Board did not deliberate during the “organizational meeting” as any discussions that may have occurred did not involve the Board’s exercise of governmental business, policy, or administration.

allegations.summary: A quorum of Board members discussed a pending application with the applicant before the July 25, 2023 meeting opened, outside any posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board deliberated outside of a meeting when a quorum of members discussed the application with the applicant prior to the start of the July 25, 2023, meeting.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly deliberated outside a meeting about cancelling the August 8, 2023 meeting, through the Chair's scheduling decision.
allegations.key_passage: As such, discussions that relate solely to scheduling do not constitute deliberation.

allegations.summary: Second complaint alleged the Board failed to elect a chair or clerk as required by G.L. c. 40A, § 12.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law and we decline to review it.

remedy: Revise the minutes of the July 25, 2023 meeting within 30 days of the date of the letter.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
